  grasp of what the aliens are telling people. Henriksen, now
  working in St. John=92s, Newfoundland, recently earned her masters
  degree in anthropology from SFU. For her thesis, Alien
  Encounters: A close analysis of personal accounts of
  extraterrestrial experiences, Henrikson interpreted the written
  stories of 60 men and women who claim to have met with alien
  life forms.
  Although Henriksen says she is "personally highly skeptical"
  that aliens have been in touch with earthlings, her research
  "suggested that aliens bring a pretty standard message of hope
  and goodwill. There are four key themes to their messages. The
  first is that the person receiving the message is in some way
  chosen or special=97they have a purpose in life. Second is the
  message that that person is not alone; someone cares for them.
  Third is the idea that the world is at risk, but the recipient
  has the power to affect change. And finally, there are few
  aliens who bring malevolent messages, but they are definitely in
  the minority."
  As an undergraduate archaeology student at the University of
  Alberta, Henriksen minored in religious studies, and developed
  "an intense interest in faith and belief systems." Her interest
  in aliens was sparked during a summer road trip with a friend
  who was reading about a particular group of highly sociable
  aliens known as Pleiadians.
  "From an academic point of view, it=92s easy to dismiss marginal
  or fringe groups like the people who believe they=92ve been
  abducted by aliens," says Henriksen. "It=92s much more work to try
  to understand where they are coming from, what motivates them.
  But that=92s what anthropology is all about: studying those who
  aren=92t us so that we are better able to understand ourselves."
  Henriksen believes the "whole phenomenon is a direct reflection
  of the search for meaning in western society." She notes that
  along with the increase in reported alien encounters, "there has
  been a correspondent explosion in new religious movements in
  North America." She sees a "direct link" between alien believers
  and the followers of New Age and evangelical Christians: "they
  are all vibrant communities, deeply committed and vocal, with an
  active web presence, and frequent opportunities for social get-
  togethers."
  A member of the United Church of Canada herself, Henriksen says
  she prefers her "religion old, tried and true, with a solid


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2002/sep/m26-009.shtml[11/12/2011 17:56:39]
Alien's Message Hope & Goodwill To Humanity

  theological foundation and a long history." Still, she was
  impressed by the faith evident in the stories of alien contact:
  "I think it=92s just another way of making sense of pain and
  loneliness. Everyone wants to find to the place where they
  belong." Even if it is in outer space.
  -30-

  THE US GOVERNMENT AND IRAQI BIOLOGICAL WEAPONS
  "Did the United States help Iraq to acquire the building blocks
  of biological weapons during the Iran-Iraq War? Are we, in
  fact, now facing the possibility of reaping what we have sown?"
  When Senator Robert Byrd posed those bothersome questions to
  Defense Secretary Donald Rumsfeld at a September 19 hearing,
  Rumsfeld dismissed the matter with a curt "I doubt it."
  But in fact there is abundant documentary and reportorial
  evidence to demonstrate that "the U.S. Government provided
  nearly two dozen viral and bacterial samples to Iraqi scientists
  in 1985--samples that included the plague, botulism, and
  anthrax, among other deadly diseases."
  A 1995 letter from then-director of the Centers for Disease
  Control David Satcher to Sen. Donald Riegle itemizes "all
  biological materials, including viruses, retroviruses, bacteria,
  and fungi, which CDC provided to the government of Iraq from
  October 1, 1984, through October 13, 1993."
  Sen. Byrd assembled all of the key evidence -- the Satcher
  letter, a recent Newsweek article by Christopher Dickey and Evan
  Thomas, the transcript of his exchange with Secretary Rumsfeld,
  and an excerpt from a 1994 Senate Banking Committee report --
    and inserted this information in the Congressional Record on
  September 20. See:
  http://www.fas.org/irp/congress/2002_cr/s092002.html
  Columnist Robert D. Novak discussed the issue in a Washington
  Post op-ed column today, available here:
  http://www.townhall.com/columnists/robertnovak/rn20020926.shtml
  The prevailing US attitude toward Iraq during those years was
  articulated in President George H.W. Bush's upbeat National
  Security Directive 26 of October 2, 1989 on "U.S. Policy Toward
  the Persian Gulf":
  "Normal relations between the United States and Iraq would serve
  our longer-term interests and promote stability in both the Gulf
  and the Middle East. The United States Government should
  propose economic and political incentives for Iraq to moderate
  its behavior and to increase our influence with Iraq."



http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2002/sep/m27-002.shtml[11/12/2011 17:56:42]
Secrecy News -- 09/26/02

  "At the same time, the Iraqi leadership must understand that any
  illegal use of chemical and/or biological weapons will lead to
  economic and political sanctions, for which we would seek the
  broadest possible support from our allies and friends," the
  previous President Bush wrote.
  A copy of NSD 26, declassified in 1999, is posted here:
  http://www.fas.org/irp/offdocs/nsd/nsd26.pdf
  The gathering momentum for a US war with Iraq signals the
  decline of American democracy, argues columnist Michael Kinsley
  today.
  Public deliberation about whether to go to war has been crippled
  by the fact that "crucial information for an independent
  decision is unavailable to us... We aren't capable of answering
  the actual questions at hand: Is Saddam Hussein an imminent
  threat to our national and personal security, and is a war to
  remove him from power the only way to end that threat?"
  See "Ours Not to Reason Why" by Michael Kinsley in Slate
  Magazine:
  http://slate.msn.com/?id71538

  GAO REPORT ON FOIA ACTIVITY
  The General Accounting Office has issued a comprehensive new
  report on implementation of the Freedom of Information Act in
  dozens of federal agencies, noting that "backlogs of pending
  requests governmentwide are substantial and growing, indicating
  that agencies are falling behind in processing requests."
  The Department of Energy, for example, took 16 days to process
  simple requests in 1999, but needed 211 days in 2001. More
  complex requests took DOE a median of 55 days to process in
  1999, but required a dysfunctional 1,788 days by 2001, the GAO
  found.
  The impact of September 11 was assessed differently by agency
  officials and FOIA requesters, the GAO said.
  "Agency officials characterized the effects on FOIA
  implementation as relatively minor, except for mail delays
  associated with the anthrax problem. In contrast, members of
  the requester community expressed general concern about
  information dissemination and access to government information
  in light of removal of information from government Web sites
  after September 11."
  See GAO Report GAO-02-493, "Update on Implementation of the 1996
  Electronic Freedom of Information Act Amendments" (in a massive
  2 MB PDF file) here:
  http://www.fas.org/sgp/foia/gao02493.pdf

  SENATE CLEARS 2003 INTEL AUTHORIZATION BILL
  "I can assure my colleagues that this bill provides a
  significant increase in funding to the U.S. intelligence
  community," said Sen. Richard Shelby.
  So assured, the Senate proceeded September 25 to approve the
  2003 intelligence authorization bill on a voice vote. See:
  http://www.fas.org/irp/congress/2002_cr/s092502.html
  The fifth public hearing of the congressional joint inquiry into
  September 11 today featured perfunctory testimony from former
  FBI counterterrorism official Dale Watson. See:
  http://www.fas.org/irp/congress/2002_hr/092602watson.html

    >story about another researcher, this one at Lawrence Berkeley
    >National Laboratory, who also falsified and fabricated data in
    >the discovery of Element 118 (which subsequently decayed to
    >Element 116), a discovery which was later retracted.
  This got a fair amount of coverage in the SF Bay Area. The guy
  was unceromoniously booted out.
    >Yes, many scientists have made honest mistakes or allow their
    >personal biases or misjudgements to lead to erroneous conclusions
    >or findings which are false. Fortunately there does not seem to
    >be many dishonest ones but the few we now know of may only be the
    >ones that got caught. I think there are many more - recall the
    >many papers which were published by scientists at many different
    >research institutions who confirmed the discovery of N rays.
  By chance, last week I was watching local PBS TV which replayed
  a program on scientific fraud. One of the scientists interviewed
  said he could go on for hours about all the cases that he
  personally knew about where scientists doctored or made up data.
  The program mentioned how even notables such as Isaac Newton
  manufactured data in order to discredit a rival's theory. This
  was fraud for petty personal reasons.
  Another example was Gregor Mendel, whose genetics data was too
  perfect. In his case, he may have doctored his numbers to make a
  stronger case for his laws of genetics. He got ignored for
  another 40 years anyway for all his troubles.
  Most fraud today, according to the program, is caused by the
  highly competitive scramble for limited grant money,
  professional recognition, job promotions, and tenured positions
  at universities. A major measure used of a scientist's
  competence or value is the number of research papers they turn
  out, hence the "publish or perish" syndrome.
  Sometimes establishment science is guilty of perpetrating its
  own brand of scientific fraud. An example given was the debacle
  surrounding Pons and Fleischman's announcement of cold fusion.
  At first Pons and Fleischman were accused of bad science or
  fraud by the establishment. They lost their funding and had
  their careers severely damaged by the establishment
  condemnations of their research. This also had the effect of
  frightening off many other researchers. In the meantime, big-
    money "hot fusion" and standard nuclear energy killed off a
  potential competitor. Professional jealousy and rigid thinking
  by other scientists also no doubt played a big part.
  According to the program, it is now generally accepted that P &
  F were definitely on to something, though not necessarily "cold
  fusion" per se. Under the right experimental conditions,
  electrolysis of water does yield more energy than put in. But


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2002/sep/m27-003.shtml[11/12/2011 17:56:42]
Re: Falsified and Fabricated Data - Rudiak

  the self-righteous scientific attacks on P & F's anomalous
  findings set back research 10-15 years. It's not a pretty story.
  And it is by no means the only example in the history of science
  where the "establishment" killed off promising lines of
  research. Commonly this is the doing of petty "graybeards" in
  the fields whom the less-prominent are fearful of crossing.
  There is very much a sociological and economic aspect to science
  that often goes overlooked. What is considered scientific "fact"
  is very much determined by consensus (and also where the money
  is). And the consensus can change over the years. In the
  meantime, scientists who cross the consensus often do so at
  their own career and economic peril. Sometimes they are truly
  nothing but fringe cases, but sometimes they are simply ahead of
  the times.
    >There are no such thing as N rays...but the jury is still out
    >regarding a UFO crash near Roswell in 1947.
  In the case of the Mogul balloon trajectory hoax of Charles
  Moore which I recently exposed, there was no apparent economic
  motivation. Moore wasn't competing for a position or grant. It
  had more to do with his personal biases regarding the Roswell
  incident and maybe his ego.
  The fact that Moore seriously fudged his data regarding his
  Mogul balloon doesn't directly tell us anything about whether a
  flying disk crashed near Roswell. It does, however, tell us that
  his lost Mogul Flight #4 was very unlikely to have reached the
  Foster Ranch, given the existing wind data. Thus it seriously
  lessens the probability of the current official explanation
  (Mogul) as being the correct explanation.
  The other thing it tells us is that the skeptics and debunkers
  live by a double standard and are completely unwilling to
  condemn their own for fraud. But we knew that already.
  For more on Moore's hoaxing, see:
  www.roswellproof.homestead.flight4_trajectory.html
  www.roswellproof.homestead.flight4and5_changes.html

  Home - Symbols - Archetypal Symbols
  Archetypal Symbols
  "Carl Jung began to evolve his theory of archetypes around 1910
  while working with patients at the Burgh=F6lzli Mental Hospital.
  Noting the presence of universal symbols from religion and
  mythology in the dreams and fantasies of uneducated patients,
  who would have had no conscious way of learning them, he
  concluded that these images belonged to a part of the
  unconscious not derived from personal experience. Jung proposed
  that universal images and ideas can be passed from generation to
  generation like biological traits, and he formulated the concept
  of the collective unconscious, whose contents become conscious
  when called forth by appropriate experiences in one's life."


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2002/sep/m27-005.shtml[11/12/2011 17:56:44]
Symbols

  Gale Encyclopedia of Psychology, 2nd ed. Gale Group, 2001.
  In 1999, Zo=EB started working with the C.G. Jung Institute's
  Archive for Research in Archetypal Symbolism, known as ARAS.
  ARAS was beginning to put together a dictionary of symbols based
  on images of ancient and modern art. Over a two-year period, Zo=EB
  worked on a dozen entries for the dictionary's initial draft. In
  late 2001, it was decided that most of the entries should be
  written by Jungian analysts.
  Through this work, Zo=EB became well-acquainted with many of the
  texts on symbolism, such as Ad de Vries "Dictionary of Symbols
  and Imagery," Mircea Eliade's "The Encyclopedia of Religion,"
  James Hastings' "Encyclopaedia of Religion and Ethics," and Jean
  Chevalier & Alain Gheerbrant's "A Dictionary of Symbols."
  Ancestor =A4 Boat =A4 Incense =A4 Olive Tree
  Purse =A4 Smoke =A4 Third Eye =A4 Thistle
  Tobacco =A4 Umbilical Cord =A4 Urine =A4 Werewolf

  Symbolism.

  Testament perspective.

   And you're not alone. There are many people who make-up
   abduction stories and for as many reasons as there are
   individuals. Although I don't count you because, a. you told
   everybody up-front that it was made up, and b. you did it in
   order to have a ready made skeleton for you to hang real 'facts'
   on in your book. In your case it was a literary tool or device.
   I must say that I quite enjoyed the story you made up. You did
   such a good job that you even had me wondering about you. And I
   like to think that I'm hard to fool. So much for that theory. ;)
   As I stated to EBK and Victor Viggiani on last Saturday's
   edition of 'Strange Days... Indeed', approximately one in ten
   (10 to 15%) of the cases that have been reported to me over the
   years, turn out to be good candidates for further investigation.
   The way I figure it, the only reason the percentage of 'good'
   cases that come my way is even that high probably has to do with
   my (former) association with a well known abduction researcher
   (Budd Hopkins) and the fact that I am an 'accessible' (publicly
   active/visible) abductee.
   To put it another way, 85 to 90% of the cases don't have enough
   'solid' material to make it past the initial screening process.
   Many are good 'anecdotal' accounts but lack any physical or
   other corroborative component (ie; multiple witnesses, ground
   trace evidence, etc.) that a researcher can actually check out.
   The most anyone can do with 90% of what is being reported is to
   check out the person who is reporting. If he/she turns out to be
   a basically sound, credible individual, the report gets 'filed'
   pending the future appearance of corroborative evidence or
   testimony from a second (reliable) source. Beyond that, there
   isn't much anyone can do in terms of actual investigation in
   most 'abduction' cases.
   If I might digress for a moment, at one time I used to refer
   'some' people to Budd and a small handful of others. But I don't
   even do that anymore. Now-a-days I wouldn't refer anybody to an
   "abduction researcher" on a dare. If I were to do so I would
   consider it a -disservice- to the individual.
   The reason?
   Most "abduction researchers" just end up hypnotizing the
   subjects, taking copious notes during the session and once they
   have what they want in hand, they leave the person to their own
   devices in terms of coping with the aftermath.
   Screw that.
   That's not 'good'; research, public service, responsible, or
   even "helping" people in trouble. Keerist, we need a group of
   professionals that are set-up and ready to deal with these
   reports/people. Someplace, somebody safe and sane that folks can
   contact without fear of having their heads screwed up even more
   than they already are. I hope I live long enough to see the day
   that such a group exists.

The Mysteries Of The Martyrs

                                   A mailing list for the study of UFO-related phenomena
                                               'Its All Here In Black & White'
    Location: UFOUpDatesList.Com > 2002 > Sep > Sep 27

                                                      The Mysteries Of The Martyrs
  From: David Acres <dacres@austarnet.com.au>
  Date: Fri, 27 Sep 2002 04:42:04 +1000
  Fwd Date: Fri, 27 Sep 2002 10:20:35 -0400
  Subject: The Mysteries Of The Martyrs

  Hello Errol and friends,
  I have too much spare time on my hands at present, as work is
  slow lately. So I decided to write this article, I hope you
  enjoy reading it as much as I enjoyed writing it. Comments are
  most welcome! :)

  THE MYSTERIES OF THE MARTYRS                    -    by David Acres
  Checking back on some old research links, I found one that I
  couldn't recall visiting. I was researching the bible/UFO
  connection at that time, & I was mainly using the King James
  version, I shelved the project before I got to the Catholic
  versions of the scriptures. I intend to continue this
  fascinating research as time permits.
  I find the following chapter both interesting & intriguing. How
  had these brave souls resisted screaming & kicking from flames &
  torture? Did someone slip them opium or some other painkiller?
  Had they fasted beforehand and exhausted themselves through
  prayer & dancing, inducing a trance-like state, like the
  circumcision rites of native tribes? Or were they truly miracles
  performed by God or His Angels?

  Chapter II.-The Wonderful Constancy of the Martyrs.
  <snip>
  ... when they were so torn with scourges, that the frame of
  their bodies, even to the very inward veins and arteries, was
  laid open, still patiently endured, while even those that stood
  by pitied and bewailed them. But they reached such a pitch of
  magnanimity, that not one of them let a sigh or a groan escape
  them; thus proving to us all that those holy martyrs of Christ,
  at the very time when they suffered such torments, were absent
  from the body, or rather, that the Lord then stood by them, and
  communed with them. [snip] For this reason the fire of their
  savage executioners appeared cool to them.
  <snip>
  If it were by God's grace alone, did He work in a purely
  spiritual way, or did He employ unknown techniques or devices,
  creating a nullified state, such as we so often hear of in
  abduction reports? I suppose the readers choice of explanations
  here, determines whether their faith and/or their mind, can
  allow them to accept that God could be an "ET", possibly of
  humanoid form!
  My interest was piqued, so I read on and found that there was
  also a prophetic vision.

  Chapter V. - The Departure and Vision of Polycarp.
  But the most admirable Polycarp, [snip] while he was praying, a
  vision presented itself to him three days before he was taken;


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2002/sep/m27-010.shtml[11/12/2011 17:56:47]
The Mysteries Of The Martyrs

  and, behold, the pillow under his head seemed to him on fire.
  Upon this, turning to those that were with him, he said to them
  prophetically," I must be burnt alive."

  Whilst being lead to Herod, a voice was heard in the air, not
  unlike the Apostle Pauls life-changing experience on the road to
  Damascus.

  Chapter IX.-Polycarp Refuses to Revile Christ.
  <snip>
  Now, as Polycarp was entering into the stadium, there
  came to him a voice from heaven, saying, "Be strong, and show
  thyself a man, O Polycarp!" No one saw who it was that spoke to
  him; but those of our brethren who were present heard the voice.
  <snip>

  Finally, we read of the miracle & my mind boggles with the
  possibilities!

  Chapter XV.-Polycarp is Not Injured by the Fire.
  <snip>
  When he had pronounced this amen, and so finished his
  prayer, those who were appointed for the purpose kindled the
  fire. And as the flame blazed forth in great fury, we, to whom
  it was given to witness it, beheld a great miracle, and have
  been preserved that we might report to others what then took
  place. For the fire, shaping itself into the form of an arch,
  like the sail of a ship when filled with the wind, encompassed
  as by a circle the body of the martyr. And he appeared within
  not like flesh which is burnt, but as bread that is baked, or as
  gold and silver glowing in a furnace. Moreover, we perceived
  such a sweet odour [coming from the pile], as if frankincense or
  some such precious spices had been smoking there. (DA: Baked
  flesh perhaps?)

  Chapter XVI.-Polycarp is Pierced by a Dagger.
  At length, when those wicked men perceived that his body could
  not be consumed by the fire, they commanded an executioner to go
  near and pierce him through with a dagger. And on his doing
  this, there came forth a great quantity of blood, so that the
  fire was extinguished; (DA: Boiled blood spraying out perhaps?)

  I wonder if anyone looked up, or behind? One can't help but
  wonder if there was a saucer hovering in the skies above on that
  miraculous day? Nothing conclusive can be presumed of course,
  but they are more small clues to add to many others found in the
  ancient scriptures, alluding to the possibility of early E.T.
  intervention with mankind.

  Below are the credits, including Socrates, no less!
  Chapter XXII.-Salutation.
  <snip>
  These things Caius transcribed from the copy of Irenaeus
  (who was a disciple of Polycarp), having himself been intimate
  with Irenaeus. And I Socrates transcribed them at Corinth from
  the copy of Caius. Grace be with you all.
  And I again, Pionius, wrote them from the previously written
  copy, having carefully searched into them,
  <snip>
  Source: http://www.ccel.org/fathers2/ANF-01/anf01-13.htm#P956_174048

  THE "DIRTY SECRET" ROTATION EXPERIMENT
  martian enigmas
  image: "Dirty Secret" NASA Image Rotation
  http://www.electricwarrior.com/cydonut/ewRotationNASA.jpg
  (The Electric Warrior) - Independent researchers find that image
  data described as "smoking gun" evidence for a full-scale
  subterranean cityscape on Mars has been tampered with.
  The controversial image involves a claim by The Enterprise
  Mission that data confirming extraterrestrial life was leaked to
  them under mysterious circumstances. The Electric Warrior has
  learned that the suspicious data file was in all likelihood
  already altered when acquired by one of Team Enterprise's lead
  investigators, known to the Mars anomaly community as Bullitt.
  Here's an easy experiment for you imaging specialists to try at
  home. Import the official NASA/ASU pre-release image 20020724A
  into your favorite image editor. This is the image file which
  TEM asserts is a hoax. Apply a 0.1% rotation to the left, and
  check the perimeter of your newly rotated image. You should see
  a blank space top left, and another one like it bottom right.
  The blank space seen across the top of the image that
  accompanies this article shows the result of rotating NASA's
  data. This image is a zoom from the top of the leftmost image in
  a set of images that contains IR data collected by the Odyssey
  spacecraft THEMIS instrument.
  image: TEM Image Enhancement Reveals Rotation
  http://www.electricwarrior.com/cydonut/ewRotationTEM.jpg
  The second image prepared for this article shows that the image
  which TEM touts as "real" or authentic NASA data bears a strong
  resemblance to The Electric Warrior's "Dirty Secret" rotation
  experiment.
  According to online Q&A between Bullitt and independent Mars
  anomalists, TEM's "real" TIFF data was already rotated when
  acquired. Bullitt passed along a JPEG version of what is now
  described as the "original" or unprocessed TEM source data to
  Anomalous Images (AI). A new online article published by AI
  describes the image as rotated.
  Bullitt provided untouched copies of what he acquired to key
  investigators. And if Bullitt didn't rotate the image, it was
  rotated when he got it.
  EW's version of the TEM data is not the same as that acquired by
  Anomalous Images. Rather, it is an enhanced version of TEM's
  alleged "real" TIFF data, widely disseminated following a talk
  radio broadcast in which principal investigator Richard C.


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2002/sep/m27-012.shtml[11/12/2011 17:56:48]
EW: The "Dirty Secret" Rotation Experiment

  Hoagland announced his latest bombastic evidence.
  The contrast enhancement of TEM's image reveals a mysterious
  dark gray shadow already reported by this blog. The shadow masks
  the data rotation by filling in the blank space we saw with the
  "Dirty Secret" rotation. The shadow runs all the way along the
  top of TEM's "real" data, getting progressively thinner, until
  it disappears toward the top right edge.
  THE HALF-PERCENT DATA REDUCTION
  The image rotation and the dark gray line that cuts across both
  images and plain black background are a clear indication of
  tampering, an obvious clue left by the hoaxer as a hint that
  there is something wrong with the overall TEM image. If you're
  still having trouble with that, consider the half-percent data
  reduction between the NASA/ASU and TEM versions of the file.
  The data reduction isn't hard to understand, has nothing to do
  with image compression, and you don't even have to conduct
  another experiment to see for yourself. All you have to do is
  check both NASA/ASU and TEM versions of the file and observe
  that the pixel resolution for the NASA/ASU version is 4036x1991,
  whereas the pixel resolution for the TEM version is 4036x1990.
  That's a loss of 4036 pixels and a 0.5% data reduction for the
  version that TEM calls authentic.
  What does this mean? It does not mean that the overall image was
  resized or compressed to fit a slightly smaller image
  resolution. That would be a data reduction that even TEM
  apologists would have a hard time shrugging off, and one that
  Richard Hoagland wouldn't want to explain.
  Imagine a classic pie-chart diagram with a half- percent slice
  cut out of it. That half-percent slice would necessarily cut
  across image data. Extending our pie-slice analogy, that half-
  percent of data was not actually cut out of the whole pie, but
  rather cut away from the crust.
  Those of you who remember the blank space along the bottom edge
  of the "Dirty Secret" image rotation have probably guessed that
  there is a 1x4036 row of pixels cropped away from the bottom of
  the rotated TEM image. The image hoaxer cut a line of pixels
  from the bottom of the TEM image to hide the rotation. The
  bottom edge of the tampered-with TEM image has a plain black
  background, just like the full size NASA/ASU image.
  Try it yourself. Removing the bottom line of pixels from the
  "Dirty Secret" rotation image will adequately conceal evidence
  of rotation by simply cutting it out of the picture. No need for
  a messy dark shadow along the bottom edge. That's why the TEM
  image is only 1990 pixels high.
  THE RISE OF THE TEM APOLOGISTS
  While TEM apologists cling tenaciously to the hope that the data
  is still valid and points to a bona fide city on Mars, The
  Electric Warrior suggests that the image rotation and data crop
  are way "out of spec" for an image ostensibly from NASA or the
  Arizona State University THEMIS team. Don't you suppose that the
  folks at ASU have Quality Assurance standards that would prevent
  them from releasing such an obviously flawed image?
  TEM apologists are already floating the idea that NASA passed
  questionable data to TEM in a valiant, if slipshod, effort to
  expose the truth about a speculative extraterrestrial
  civilization on Mars. It remains to be seen whether The
  Enterprise Mission seizes upon this new information and casts it
  as case for plausible deniability. As my online colleague, Mac
  Tonnies of the Cydonia Imperative has written, this isn't the
  first time that "smoking gun" evidence for artificial structures
  on Mars has been offered by TEM.
  If the hoaxer had simply cropped off the top edge of the TEM
  data, in the same way the bottom was cropped, the image
  tampering would have cut away part of the THEMIS data, and
  researchers working with the IR data would have noticed. The
  show would be over. You wouldn't be reading this article.
  Mac is really much better than I am at explaining the dramatic
  cloak-and-dagger aspects of The Enterprise Mission's online

  antics. At least he makes them sound interesting. So, if there's
  another dramatic plot twist to explain the Dirty Secret Rotation
  and the Half-Percent Data Reduction, maybe the Cydonian

  WORLDWIDE UFOPHOTO CATALOG IN PROCESS
  Please let me address this letter on behalf of the "Anomaly
  Foundation", a not-for-profit organization devoted to UFO
  research based in Spain. I refer to your readers to our URL
  <http://www.anomalia.org> We are developing the project FOTOCAT,
  to build up a worldwide catalog of UFO/IFO photographic cases, a
  census which presently runs over 2,500 entries. The objective is
  to post it freely in the internet for the benefit of all
  students when the project is finished (i.e., when it is decided
  that it has collected a truly representative sample of the
  phenomenon of UFO photography in the world).
  In addressing this letter to UFO researchers elsewhere, we are
  demanding individuals or organizations to send us any list of
  the photographic cases occurred in their countries (or if they
  can produce one to this purpose) to check our records with it,
  and also to expand them. The only information required for every
  photo case is: date, location, name of photographer (if known),
  mode (photo,film,video), and explanation (if there is one).
  Anyone's contribution will be duly acknowledged in the catalog's
  credits. This will also serve to prove that international
  cooperation in this field is really possible!
  Thank you for publishing this letter.

  From: Anthony Chippendale <anthony@thechippendales.co.uk>
  Date: Fri, 27 Sep 2002 16:38:43 +0100
  Fwd Date: Fri, 27 Sep 2002 14:07:35 -0400
  Subject: UFOn UK Closure

  After many years, I have closed down my UFO website UFOn UK
  which was at:
  www.ufon.org.uk
  The URL now points to the main UFOn website at ufon.org
  It was not an easy decision but visitor numbers to the website
  have decreased dramatically recently and I could no longer
  justify the expense of running the site. In addition, big
  constraints on my time meant I was rarely updating - perhaps one
  of the reasons why visitor numbers declined.
  Just as a point of interest, UFO articles that I have written
  are available on my personal website www.anthonyc.net - just
  click the "UFOs" link on the menu at the bottom of the page.

  It is time to deal with the 64 dollar question - the biggest
  crazy aunt in the living room.
  The questions that need to be raised in any effort to find the
  truth about a significant event related to power and money in
  the US - and answered if we are to ever find the truth of how
  our world works - are:
  1. WHAT HAS BEEN THE SIZE OF THE U. S. BLACK BUDGET OVER THE LAST 50 YEARS?
  2. WHAT ARE THE SOURCES AND USES OF FUNDS IN THE BLACK BUDGET?
  3. WHO GOVERNS AND MANAGES THE BLACK BUDGET AND OPERATIONS?

  5. IS THE WAR ON TERRORISM MOVING THE BLACK BUDGET ON BUDGET?

  that asking these questions brings up a whole pile of
  challenging uncertainty. (For background on my experience
  dealing with black budget/slush fund operations at FHA and
  Ginnie Mae at the Department of Housing and Urban Development

  researchers simply delete the existence of such uncertainty from
  their reality. That is a big mistake - again pretending that we
  do not have a very big crazy aunt sitting in the living room.

What's Up With the Black Budget?

  George Orwell once said that "Omission is the greatest lie."
  Hence, our crazy aunt has to be dealt with.
  If you listen to the Ferdinand video/audio depositions in the
  Carone/Tyree lawsuit (
  http://www.blackopradio.com/inc_archives2002.html), what you
  will hear is something I have heard many times. Carone gives his
  family the sense of all of the organized crime operations by
  CIA, Army and Mafia through the 1970's as legitimate for
  national security purposes that then got out of hand and turned
  bad in the 1980's. That is, what started out as justifiable got
  out of hand. This begs the question ---- Why Were Such
  Activities Considered Justifiable?
  The way to deal with uncertainty is with scenario design and
  probability -- ie to create a framework of the possible
  explanations with your best estimate of the plausible scenarios
  and the probability (all adding up to 100%) of each one being
  true based on intuition. Maintaining such a framework allows
  data collection on key variables and assumptions and an
  evolution to occur that can enlighten - even determine -
    concrete questions and answers over time.
  So, let me tell a story, give you my framework that I use to
  handle the fact that I do not have the answers and invite your
  framework. I am not looking to hear only what is wrong with my
  framework. I am looking to improve mine or find a better one. Or
  better inform my estimate of the probabilities that this one or
  that one is true. Hence, I invite you to put forward your
  framework for managing this uncertainty. If we had the truth of
  the issue I am going to introduce, I dare say we could get to
  the bottom of 9-11 faster.
  In 1998, I was approached by John Peterson, head of the
  Arlington Institute, a small high quality military think tank in
  Washington, DC. I had gotten to know John through Global
  Business Network and had been impressed by his intelligence,
  effectiveness and compassion. John asked me to help him with a
  high level strategic plan Arlington was planning to undertake
  for the Undersecretary of the Navy.
  At the time I was the target of an intense smear campaign that
  would lead the normal person to assume that I would be in jail
  shortly or worse. John explained that the Navy understood that
  it was all politics ---- they did not care.
  I met with a group of high level people in the military in the
  process - including the Undersecretary. According to John, the
  purpose of the plan - discussed in front of several military or
  retired military officers and former government officials--- was
  to help the Navy adjust their operations for a world in which it
  was commonly known that aliens exist and live among us.
  When John explained this purpose to me, I explained that I did
  not know that aliens existed and lived among us. John asked me
  if I would like to meet some aliens. For the only time in my
  life, I declined an opportunity to learn about something
  important. I was concerned that my efforts with Arlington could
  boomerang and be connected with the smear campaign and the
  effects that I was managing. I regret that decision. At John's
  suggestion I started to read books on the topic and read about
  25 books over the next year on the alien question, the black
  budget, and alien technology.
  I had to drop from the project due to the need to attend to
  litigation and the physical harassment and surveillance of me
  and some of the people helping me. This process ---which turned
  out to be incredibly time consuming - I now believe was
  connected with the black budget/slush fund activities connected
  with FHA and Ginnie Mae at HUD. (See, "The Myth of the Rule of
  Law") John then asked me if I would join the board of the
  Arlington Institute.
  When I attended one of my first meetings, I joined in discussion
  with about 10 people which included James Woolsey, former head
  of the CIA in the Clinton Administration, Napier Collyns,
  founder of Global Business Network and former senior Shell
  executive, Joe Firmage, John, and other members of the Arlington
  board. The main topic of discussion was whether or not the major
  project for the coming year should be a white paper on how to
  help the American people adjust to aliens existing and living

  from the FAS Project on Government Secrecy

  September 27, 2002

  **      JUSTICE DEPT PRESSES ITS FISA APPEAL
  **      FBI DIRECTOR MUELLER ON SEPTEMBER 11
  **      NEW CRS REPORTS

  JUSTICE DEPT PRESSES ITS FISA APPEAL
  In a lengthy new brief filed with the Foreign Intelligence
  Surveillance Court of Review this week, the Justice Department
  elaborated its argument that "the wall" that traditionally
  separated law enforcement and intelligence investigations has
  been torn down by the USA Patriot Act.
  The Department contends that it is now at liberty to use the
  counterintelligence procedures of the Foreign Intelligence
  Surveillance Act, which are in some respects looser than those
  used in criminal cases, even in investigations where law
  enforcement rather than counterintelligence is the principal
  purpose of an investigation.
  By enacting the USA Patriot Act last year, "Congress directly
  and unambiguously tore down the wall," according to the new
  brief. The Act "allows unfettered coordination between
  intelligence and law enforcement officials in furtherance of
  efforts to protect against espionage and international
  terrorism."
  Aspects of that interpretation of the USA Patriot Act were
  rejected by the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court in a May
  2002 decision, made public last month, and the Department has
  appealed the ruling to the FIS Court of Review.
  In arguing against "excessive judicial interference with the
  President's authority over national security matters," the
  Justice brief coyly quotes the testimony of "one witness" in a
  1978 hearing who turns out to be... Laurence Silberman, a member
  of the FIS Court of Review to whom the brief is directed.
    (Footnote 4).
  The main body of the brief is accompanied by an appendix that
  compares and contrasts the requirements of the Foreign
  Intelligence Surveillance Act and the Title III procedures for
  obtaining a wiretap in a criminal investigation.
  See the "Supplemental Brief for the United States" filed in the
  FIS Court of Review by Attorney General John Ashcroft on
  September 25 here:
  http://www.fas.org/irp/agency/doj/fisa/092502sup.html

  FBI DIRECTOR MUELLER ON SEPTEMBER 11

  Corder first latched on to me, I think we met at some MUFON
  conference. Claimed he had some abductees with interesting
  information. Seemed to be pretty credible at first, then his
  stories got wilder and wilder, involving Biblical prophecies,
  very specific current predictions which of course did not come
  true, and various other claims. He claimed that I, too, was an
  abductee, and I think Budd as well.
  Anyway, at one point he sent me a "lexicon" of exoglyphs and
  their translations - this was a symbolic language, like
  hieroglyphs. The lexicon included about 100 very basic words,
  mostly things like "river", "mountain", "sun", "animal",
  "forest", "God", etc.
  In the interest of "due process" I forwarded the lexicon to
  Budd. I called him a few days later and asked about the symbols,
  which he said were "not really close", as I figured.
  As I was trying to get Corder off my back, I chose a rather
  abrupt way to inform him of the bad news. I simply sent him a
  postcard with two symbols on it: the one for "mountain" and the
  one for "feces".
  I guess ya had to be there...

  THE "DIRTY SECRET" ROTATION EXPERIMENT
  Martian Enigmas
  image: "Dirty Secret" NASA Image Rotation
  http://www.electricwarrior.com/cydonut/ewRotationNASA.jpg
    (The Electric Warrior) - Independent researchers find that
  image data described as "smoking gun" evidence for a full-scale
  subterranean cityscape on Mars has been tampered with.
  The controversial image involves a claim by The Enterprise
  Mission that data confirming extraterrestrial life was leaked to
  them under mysterious circumstances. The Electric Warrior has
  learned that the suspicious data file was in all likelihood
  already altered when acquired by one of Team Enterprise's lead
  investigators, known to the Mars anomaly community as Bullitt.
  Here's an easy experiment for you imaging specialists to try at
  home. Import the official NASA/ASU pre-release image 20020724A
  into your favorite image editor. This is the image file which
  TEM asserts is a hoax. Apply a 0.1% rotation to the left, and
  check the perimeter of your newly rotated image. You should see
  a blank space top left, and another one like it bottom right.
  The blank space seen across the top of the image that


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2002/sep/m28-006.shtml[11/12/2011 17:57:04]
EW: Believe the Lie And Know the Truth?

  accompanies this article shows the result of rotating NASA's
  data. This image is a zoom from the top of the leftmost image in
  a set of images that contains IR data collected by the Odyssey
  spacecraft THEMIS instrument.
  image: TEM Image Enhancement Reveals Rotation
  http://www.electricwarrior.com/cydonut/ewRotationTEM.jpg
  The second image prepared for this article shows that the image
  which TEM touts as "real" or authentic NASA data bears a strong
  resemblance to The Electric Warrior's "Dirty Secret" rotation
  experiment.
  According to online Q&A between Bullitt and independent Mars
  anomalists, TEM's "real" TIFF data was already rotated when
  acquired. Bullitt passed along a JPEG version of what is now
  described as the "original" or unprocessed TEM source data to
  Anomalous Images (AI). A new online article published by AI
  describes the image as rotated.
  Bullitt provided untouched copies of what he acquired to key
  investigators. And if Bullitt didn't rotate the image, it was
  rotated when he got it.
  EW's version of the TEM data is not the same as that acquired by
  Anomalous Images. Rather, it is an enhanced version of TEM's
  alleged "real" TIFF data, widely disseminated following a talk
  radio broadcast in which principal investigator Richard C.
  Hoagland announced his latest bombastic evidence.
  The contrast enhancement of TEM's image reveals a mysterious
  dark gray shadow already reported by this blog. The shadow masks
  the data rotation by filling in the blank space we saw with the
  "Dirty Secret" rotation. The shadow runs all the way along the
  top of TEM's "real" data, getting progressively thinner, until
  it disappears toward the top right edge.
  THE HALF-PERCENT DATA REDUCTION
  The image rotation and the dark gray line that cuts across both
  images and plain black background are a clear indication of
  tampering, an obvious clue left by the hoaxer as a hint that
  there is something wrong with the overall TEM image. If you're
  still having trouble with that, consider the half-percent data
  reduction between the NASA/ASU and TEM versions of the file.
  The data reduction isn't hard to understand, has nothing to do
  with image compression, and you don't even have to conduct
  another experiment to see for yourself. All you have to do is
  check both NASA/ASU and TEM versions of the file and observe
  that the pixel resolution for the NASA/ASU version is 4036x1991,
  whereas the pixel resolution for the TEM version is 4036x1990.
  That's a loss of 4036 pixels and a 0.5% data reduction for the
  version that TEM calls authentic.
  What does this mean? It does not mean that the overall image was
  resized or compressed to fit a slightly smaller image
  resolution. That would be a data reduction that even TEM
  apologists would have a hard time shrugging off, and one that
  Richard Hoagland wouldn't want to explain.
  Imagine a classic pie-chart diagram with a half- percent slice
  cut out of it. That half-percent slice would necessarily cut
  across image data. Extending our pie-slice analogy, that half-
  percent of data was not actually cut out of the whole pie, but
  rather cut away from the crust.
  Those of you who remember the blank space along the bottom edge
  of the "Dirty Secret" image rotation have probably guessed that
  there is a 1x4036 row of pixels cropped away from the bottom of
  the rotated TEM image. The image hoaxer cut a line of pixels
  from the bottom of the TEM image to hide the rotation. The
  bottom edge of the tampered-with TEM image has a plain black
  background, just like the full size NASA/ASU image.
  Try it yourself. Removing the bottom line of pixels from the
  "Dirty Secret" rotation image will adequately conceal evidence
  of rotation by simply cutting it out of the picture. No need for
  a messy dark shadow along the bottom edge. That's why the TEM
  image is only 1990 pixels high.

  BELIEVE THE LIE, AND KNOW THE TRUTH?
  In an online article that coincided with a live talk radio
  broadcast, TEM's Richard C. Hoagland alleged that the official
  THEMIS data hosted by NASA/ASU was a deliberately degraded
  fraud. At that time, TEM put forth another version of the THEMIS
  file saying theirs was the "real" or authentic Mars data.
  The following week, TEM said that Bullitt may have been "bamfed"
  or redirected to a special data server when he acquired their
  version of the file. Additional images released at that time
  allegedly showed an elaborate subterranean city complex below
  the surface on Mars, based on further processing of TEM's "real"
  data.
  One of the principal characters in TEM's online drama was said
  to be Arizona State University software manager Noel Gorelick,
  who goes by the online name Bamf. As told by The Enterprise
  Mission, Bamf led Bullitt to the controversial data file.
  Gorelick told MSNBC that he occasionally provided online advice
  to imaging specialists on TEM's message board, saying, "Any role
  ascribed to me beyond that is totally false." So, Bamf denies
  any further involvement with the circumstances involving
  Bullitt's "real" data file download on July 25.
  MSNBC's Alan Boyle speculated whether some prankster might have
  spoofed Bafm's identity on the Internet and led Bullitt astray.
  The point of this article is not that the data rotation and
  image crop cannot be undone or worked around. The point is that
  the obvious image tampering should cause you to question whether
  The Enterprise Mission really acquired their data from NASA or
  ASU.
  Alternative science investigators would say the file's
  provenance is called into question. TEM would have you believe
  the suspicious data was leaked under mysterious circumstances.

  THE RISE OF THE TEM APOLOGISTS
  While TEM apologists cling tenaciously to the hope that the data
  is still valid and points to a bona fide city on Mars, The
  Electric Warrior suggests that the image rotation and data crop
  are way "out of spec" for an image ostensibly from NASA or the
  Arizona State University THEMIS team. Don't you suppose that the
  folks at ASU have Quality Assurance standards that would prevent
  them from releasing such an obviously flawed image?
  The TEM image, with its presentation flaws, doesn't look
  professional. It isn't NASA quality.
  TEM apologists are already floating the idea that NASA passed
  questionable data to TEM in a valiant, if slipshod, effort to
  expose the truth about a speculative extraterrestrial
  civilization on Mars. As if to say NASA made it look bad, so
  they could deny it, but it still reveals a subterranean city on
  Mars.
  It remains to be seen whether The Enterprise Mission seizes upon
  this new information and casts it as case for plausible
  deniability. As my online colleague, Mac Tonnies of the Cydonia
  Imperative has written, this isn't the first time that "smoking
  gun" evidence for artificial structures on Mars has been offered
  by TEM.
  If the hoaxer had simply cropped off the top edge of the TEM
  data, in the same way the bottom was cropped, the image
  tampering would have cut away part of the THEMIS data, and
  researchers working with the IR data would have noticed. The
  show would be over. You wouldn't be reading this article.
  Mac is really much better than I am at explaining the dramatic
  cloak-and-dagger aspects of The Enterprise Mission's online
  antics. At least he makes them sound interesting. So, if there's
  another dramatic plot twist to explain the Dirty Secret Rotation
  and the Half-Percent Data Reduction, maybe the Cydonian
  Imperative will want to take a shot at it.

  During the third of those sessions I was recalling how a small,
  whitish, "alien" had led me into a small room and positioned me
  in front of a large, curved screen of some kind.
  Upon this screen there suddenly appeared a large symbol, it
  resembled a French Fleur de Lys. The only real difference
  between it and the French version is; the points of the one I
  was shown were all more like upward-pointing flames.
  Located just inside the tip of each petal of the 'Fleur de Lys'
  was a single glyph. (letter, character) I was ordered by this
  little being to; "Study and remember." That three word phrase
  was repeated inside my head three times. There was no mistaking
  the tone of command either. It was very emphatic.
  After Budd brought me out of the trance-state, he asked me if I
  could reproduce (draw) the symbol and the characters I had been
  shown. "No problem, I'm an artist," I told him. He handed me a
  pencil and a large yellow legal pad and I gave him what he asked
  for.
  I have only seen the blood run out of a man's face twice in my
  life. It is an eerie thing to witness. One of those times was
  the moment Budd took a look at what I had drawn. You can't fake
  a reaction like that. It made the hairs on neck and arms stand
  on end. He mumbled something rapid-fire at me that sounded like;
  'Don't move. Stay right here... I'll be right back." And off he
  went.
  He was gone about five minutes. When he returned he was winded
  and clutching a purple, plastic file folder to his chest. He sat
  down next to me, handed me the yellow piece of paper I had just
  drawn the symbols on, and he placed the purple folder in front
  of me. He didn't say a word.
  I opened the folder and I saw that it contained several (about
  six) different sized pieces of paper with 'writing' on them. On
  closer inspection I saw that they resembled the same type of
  symbols that I had just reproduced. Then the real shockeroo
  came, on the top page in front of me I spotted one of the
  symbols I had just drawn. Not simply similar or close in
  appearance, but a dead-on match. The _same_ character that
  appeared on my yellow paper.
  Then I spotted another dead-match on the second page. As I
  flipped through the pages tears started to run down my face and
  all I could think to ask Budd was, "What the hell is this? Where
  did you get it?" His response was of no comfort to me and only
  served to deepen a malaise that had taken hold of my gut. I felt
  physically sick, like I wanted to throw up. I also felt terribly
  confused.
  How could these people, people I had never met or even heard of,
  reproduce the same characters that I had just drawn. All of the
  papers in the folder were dated and signed. Some had been
  written years ago. This was no mere coincidence.
  I am not Jean Dixon. There is no f*****g way I just pulled that
  stuff out of the air. Not only did I recall seeing those symbols
  for the first time aboard a UFO, but that's where everybody else
  (from the folder) saw their symbols too.
  Jim, I just sat there sobbing like a child. I didn't know what
  to think. It was such a world shattering confirmation for me
  that it left me devastated. It took weeks for me to recover from

  Hi List,
  To address some of the recent posts on alleged alien symbols.
  Archetypal imagery is one of the most misinterpreted notions on
  the planet and this is stressed by psychologists who claim
  expertise. Jung edited a book in 1961, which was an attempt to
  begin understanding archetypal symbols and this was co-written
  by a few eminent psychologists entitled 'Man and his Symbols.'
  Rather than be a tome filled with technical terms, it was a book
  that was written to be accessible to the general reader and that
  would be a good place for anyone to make a start.
  There are many archetypal symbols and some of these are relevant
  to the study of alleged alien motifs and language. We are
  examining this aspect carefully.
  As to the question regarding crop circle similarities; there are
  a few which we have come across.
  I would like to see Jim Speiser's lexicon of alleged alien
  semiotics from Corder - if he still has a copy?
  In reference to Dick Hall's statement about not having time to
  search through archetypal images to compare with alleged alien
  symbols; I have a suggestion. Dick please sort out and send any
  examples to me; and I will place these in a data set where this
  will happen anyway and I will let you know what the results are?
  It is actually better to do it this way round rather than the
  other!

  Best Regards
  Gary Anthony

                                   A mailing list for the study of UFO-related phenomena

                                            Cincinnati Enquirer on UFO Conference
  From: Kenny Young <ufo@fuse.net>
  Date: Sat, 28 Sep 2002 08:02:32 -0700
  Fwd Date: Sat, 28 Sep 2002 08:35:20 -0400
  Subject: Cincinnati Enquirer on UFO Conference

  UFO conference
  Truth is out there, in Mason
  The Cincinnati Enquirer
  Saturday, September 28, 2002
  By Karen Samples Gutierrez
  We are not alone, folks.
  Sharing our world are alien-implant investigators, weirdology
  editors and Congressional candidates running on UFO platforms.
  (As in ideas, not saucer-shaped heels.)
  Actually, there's only about one each of these people. But
  today, all will gather in the same place: Kings Island, for the
  39th annual National UFO Conference.
  These are the folks who keep America safe from getting too
  skeptical. Turns out Ohio is fertile ground.
  Since "98, 517 UFO sightings have been reported in the Buckeye
  State, which is, on average, 102 more than in seven states of
  similar size. This according to statistics from the National UFO
  Reporting Center.
  The conference has been held more times in Ohio than any place
  else. Co-founder James Moseley says Ohio always has had more UFO
  groups than other states its size.
  Of course, these include the Roundtown UFO Society, which
  consists of two people in Circleville. But still.
  "It's sort of Middle America," Mr. Moseley says. "Maybe people
  have nothing better to do."
  He lives in Key West, Fla., so he must have some other excuse.
  Mysterious events
  This year's conference organizer is Kenny Young of Florence. Mr.
  Young spends his free time investigating suspicious happenings.
  For instance, on Feb. 2 a "chevron-shaped" object was supposedly
  seen over the Ohio River near Maysville. After many calls, Mr.
  Young finally spoke with a guard at the East Bend power plant
  who indeed recorded said object in his log. The officer couldn't
  tell what it was. Mr. Young tried to find other witnesses
  through a classified ad, but the Maysville paper wouldn't print
  it.
  Mr. Young usually uncovers ordinary explanations for UFOs, which
  he documents on his Web site, http://home.fuse.net/ufo
  "It's not a matter of belief," he says. "It's a matter of
  investigative curiosity."
  He caught the bug as a first-grader in 1973, one of the glory
  years for seeing things. Back in the '50s and '70s, UFOs were


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2002/sep/m28-013.shtml[11/12/2011 17:57:08]
Cincinnati Enquirer on UFO Conference

  even considered newsworthy.
  Now it's all another X-Files rerun. "Abductees" know exactly how
  they're supposed to say the aliens look, and crop circles have
  become absurdly complex.
  "There's something naive and nostalgic about it in the early
  days," says Lance Moody, a Mason skeptic who follows the UFO
  community.
  If he can squeeze it in between his kids' soccer games, Mr.
  Moody will stop by Kings Island today to hear the odds of alien
  invasion.
  Speakers include Stephen Bassett of Maryland, the Congressional
  candidate who wants to stop government cover-ups.
  Others will be more skeptical, addressing hoaxes and scientific
  findings about life on other planets.
  Mr. Young welcomes anyone with a little curiosity about the
  universe. That's what we've lost, he says =97 not gullibility so
  much as the simple pleasure of gazing skyward.

  End of article

  Hi List, Steven,
  I have Mario Pazzaglini's 'Symbolic Messages' it has some very
  pertinent material for this topic and makes valid points for
  anyone undertaking a study, including the mention of archetypal
  symbols. It was what inspired me to take a further look at this
  aspect.
  What 'Symbolic Messages' doesn't have, in regard to the samples
  cited and those used in this study, is an analysis of the
  'structure' of alleged alien languages.
  Pazzaglini tried to incorporate everything else but neglected
  this one important and crucial part, despite the many other
  linguistic components cited.
  Demonstrably this must be where Pazzaglini's linguistic
  knowledge ends and is one of several areas that need
  undertaking, not least by linguists and cryptanalysts.
  If a linguist was to study Pazzaglini's book this is the first
  thing he/she would point out, lack of structure analysis.

  Best Regards
  Gary Anthony

                                              UFO Sighting Over Montreal, Quebec
  From: Brian Vike <yogibear@bulkley.net>
  Date: Sat, 28 Sep 2002 08:20:13 -0700
  Fwd Date: Sat, 28 Sep 2002 14:26:38 -0400
  Subject: UFO Sighting Over Montreal, Quebec

  Hi List
  Here is a report I received by way of email this morning. I
  pasted as is, except for the witnesses name and phone number
  which has been deleted from the letter.
  Take care
  Brian
  HUFOBCC
  ---
  UFO Sighting in Montreal, Quebec, Canada
  Location: Champlain Bridge
  Time: 7:40 pm
  Date: Friday, September 27, 2002
  I was driving on the Champlain Bridge going South. It was
  raining. I was in the middle lane almost on the highest point
  of the bridge when I saw from the corner of my eye, what looked
  liked a plane flying extremely low, coming from my right.
  As I was getting to the highest point of the bridge (under the
  metal structure) the lights flew over the bridge in a horizontal
  flight pattern (it slowed down when crossing over the bridge) I
  then had a good look at the light formation. It then increased
  speed, where it broke its flight line at a right angle going up
  into the sky over St-Lambert.
  As I was driving under the structure, I realized that what I was
  looking at, was not a plane. The light formation was not a
  plane or anything else I had seen before. It seemed that cars
  slowed down. I was stunned. What I'd like to know, did you get
  reports from others? Did anyone else see this thing? I could
  not have been the only one, who else saw this?
  Description of UFO:
  The basic shape of the craft looked like a small square which is
  wider at the top, almost like a truncated triangle or a
  geometric 'U' that widens half way up. The whole thing was the
  size of the small truck.
  I have a feeling I was looking at the end of the craft because I
  saw a light formation with lights that were circular, flat and
  red, which you would of seen at the back old car in the fifties.
  The lights were not 'bulb like' but rather extremely flat, and
  the diameter of these lights were the size of a dinnerplate.
  Four lights on each side and three at the bottom of the
  geometric 'U'.
  Please let me know if you hear of any other reports from this
  sight. All of a sudden this thing seems very important to me, I
  just want to know that others have seen this too and I am not
  losing my mind.
  Email Report
